about: Every number and named source this video shows or says, with its source. Each page opened and re-read on Oct 28, 2026 (Central); the note is the page's own sentence. Checked by the facts gate against the source pages.

firstVisit.title: Follow-Ups 101: Back 2 Basics
firstVisit.publisher: ServiceTitan (blog, webinar recap by Mike LaFollette)
firstVisit.kind: vendor data, method not shown; said on screen and in voice as ServiceTitan's own data
firstVisit.note: Page description: "Only 37% of estimates close on the first visit." Body: "Burgess says most in-home sales don't close on the first visit. In fact, ServiceTitan data shows only 37% convert immediately, which leaves the majority of opportunities dependent on" follow-up.
firstVisit.doNotUse: the same page's 64%, 72% and 87% figures (KNOWLEDGE.md do-not-use list)

speedStudy.title: Speed Is a Signal: When Faster Replies Increase Hiring Likelihood
speedStudy.publisher: Management Science (UC San Diego news summary, Jun 25, 2026)
speedStudy.authors: Einav Hart, On Amir, Eric VanEpps, Ovul Sezer
speedStudy.value: qualitative: fast replies lose their appeal when people believe they are automated or AI-written
speedStudy.note: "In the experiments, faster replies lost their appeal when recipients believed them to be generated automatically or by an AI." The study is about first replies (11.6 million Fiverr interactions plus experiments), so the script says "fast replies", not "follow-ups".

cadence.title: Quote Follow-Up Email Templates: 7 Examples to Close More Jobs
cadence.daysNote: 24 to 48 hours, said as "a day or two"
cadence.note: First follow-up "should land in their inbox within two days after sending the quote"; "you can send your next email one week after sending your initial quote"; "it's best to send your final follow-up 24-48 hours before the quote expires"; "If you haven't heard back after your third follow-up, it's OK to close the file and move on."

nineWord.title: The 9-Word Email: The Complete Guide by Its Creator
nineWord.note: Body: "Are you still looking for [the thing they inquired about]?" "You're asking a question, not making an announcement." "That's the whole email. No signature. No pitch. No links."
